title: Tenant-consistent windowed exports with checkpoint leases
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Scheduled customer usage exports currently rely on monolithic job runs that: 1) produce large single CSV blobs per tenant, 2) have poor resumability on failures, and 3) make tenant isolation and prioritization awkward during congestion. We see frequent operator intervention for partial retries and S3 multipart inconsistencies for large tenants.

Goal: Replace the single-run export model with a windowed export pipeline that writes durable, ordered CSV windows per tenant and uses a lightweight checkpoint-lease mechanism to provide safe resumability, hot-restart after transient failures, and tenant-scoped backpressure. This should reduce end-to-end retry complexity, improve small-tenant latency for scheduled preview runs, and make high-volume tenants more predictable without blocking other customers.

Design highlights (proposal):
- Windowed segments: Exports for a tenant are split into fixed-time windows (configurable; default 1hr) that generate small CSV shards (example: tenant-YYYYMMDD-HH-window-0001.csv). Windows are append-only and independent for resumability.
- Checkpoint lease table: A central leases table (Postgres table in console DB) maintains per-tenant export run metadata: current-window, last-committed-offset, lease-holder-id, lease-expiry. Workers acquire a short TTL lease before writing a window. If the lease expires or holder fails, another worker may continue after reconciling offsets.
- Idempotent uploads: Each shard is uploaded as a multipart S3 object with deterministic keys and an export-manifest.json that lists constituent shards and checksums. Uploads include client-side checksum and server-side verification. Incomplete multipart uploads are reconciled by a background janitor using manifest+etag heuristics.
- Coalescing & small-file strategy: For tiny tenants, we coalesce multiple contiguous windows into a single composite CSV to reduce S3 object explosion. Coalescing is recorded in manifest entries to preserve replayability.
- Webhook delivery model: For webhook subscribers we publish per-window delivery events containing an idempotency token (export_run_id + window_id + seq). Delivery service retries are bounded by tenant priority and backpressure; webhook consumer acknowledges via delivery receipt endpoint which updates per-window delivery status in the leases table.
- Backpressure & prioritization: Scheduler enforces tenant-level concurrency and global export concurrency. High-throughput tenants can be assigned reserved slots; low priority tenants are gated to keep SLAs for dedicated customers.
- Observability: New Grafana dashboards for window latency, lease-acquisition waits, incomplete multipart count, and per-tenant export cost estimates. Traces correlate lease acquisition -> CSV generation -> multipart upload -> manifest commit -> webhook delivery.

Implementation notes:
- Storage: Use existing console Postgres for leases and manifest metadata; shard keys by tenant_id to avoid hotspots. Long-term manifest/archive pointers are written to Redshift for reporting.
- Worker model: Stateless workers run in k8s with leadership via lease acquisition. Workers write CSV shards to an intermediate blobstore (S3 staging with object lifecycle) then commit manifest rows in a single transaction to mark window complete.
- Resumption flow: On worker restart, process checks leases table; if an in-progress window's lease is expired and last-committed-offset < window-length, the new worker picks up from offset and resumes multipart upload or re-creates missing shard pieces.
- Security/Compliance: All S3 objects are server-side encrypted with the tenant-specific KMS key where applicable. Access logs and audit trail preserved in console audit log stream.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal-only run for 2 week using non-critical tenants; enable window size=6h to reduce churn.
2) Beta: opt-in customers and previews in console; add coalescing flag.
3) GA: Default scheduled exports flip to windowed flow with a migration job that converts legacy manifests into windowed manifests (copy + manifest link).

Open questions / design trade-offs:
- Lease TTL length: shorter TTL reduces lock time but increases worker thrash. Initial value proposed: 30s + backoff-based renewals.
- Leases in Postgres vs distributed KV: Postgres is simplest but could be a single point during heavy export churn. Consider Redis/Consul if we see pressure.
- Cost trade-off for coalescing: increased read complexity vs fewer objects. We'll expose coalescing thresholds per-customer.

Acceptance criteria:
- Resumable export across worker restarts for > 50GB tenants with no human intervention in 95% of test runs.
- Manifest-based verification ensures no partial objects considered committed.
- Webhook deliveries include idempotency tokens and can be retried without duplication.
- Dashboards surface lease contention and incomplete uploads with alerts.

Rollout steps and feature flags:
- feature.flags.windowed_exports = off (default)
- feature.flags.window_coalescing = off (default)
- Controlled rollout by org ID list and quota thresholds.

Docs and artifacts:
- Implementation design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/EXPORTS-Windowed-Strategy
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/exporter/pull/1284
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/exports/usage-export-latency

Notes: This ticket focuses on orchestration, leases, manifest format, and S3 resiliency. Separate tickets will handle UI preview flows, billing attribution for windowed exports, and Redshift consumption optimization.
